title: Non-relativistic Floquet Conformal Field Theory
authors: Diptarka Das, Sumit R. Das, Arnab Kundu, Krishnendu Sengupta
abstract: We develop a formalism for studying Floquet dynamics for systems with {\it non-relativistic} conformal invariance in $d$ spatial dimensions. Our analysis indicates the existence of two dynamical phases, hyperbolic and elliptic, separated by a parabolic transition surface. We demonstrate this by studying the expectation value of a conformal generator in the many body ground state during the drive, as well as the fidelity of this state. Stroboscopically, they behave exponentially in the hyperbolic phase, show oscillatory behavior in the elliptic phase, and exhibit power-law on the transition surface. Our analysis is completely universal and can be directly applied to several systems including trapped fermions near unitarity and resonant anyons. The former can provide experimental signatures of these dynamical phases. We also comment on a holographic perspective of such driven non-relativistic CFTs and demonstrate that the hyperbolic phase is associated with a timelike stationary-limit surface, such as an ergosphere, in the bulk, while the parabolic phase corresponds to an extremal Killing horizon.
summary: This paper develops a universal formalism to study Floquet dynamics in quantum systems with non-relativistic conformal invariance. It identifies three distinct dynamical regimes—hyperbolic, elliptic, and parabolic—diagnosed via stroboscopic measurements of observables like state fidelity. The results are significant because they connect these quantum phases to deep concepts in general relativity, such as ergospheres and extremal Killing horizons.
main_problem: Developing a formalism to study Floquet dynamics for quantum systems exhibiting non-relativistic conformal invariance.
main_result: The analysis predicts three universal dynamical phases—hyperbolic, elliptic, and parabolic—characterized by the stroboscopic evolution of observables. Furthermore, it establishes a holographic link where the hyperbolic phase corresponds to an ergosphere in the bulk geometry.
method: The study uses Floquet theory applied to Hamiltonians derived from an SO(2, 1) algebra, mapping the dynamics onto the Ermakov-Pinney equation for analysis.
model_or_system: The model concerns periodically driven strongly correlated quantum systems, with trapped fermions near unitarity and resonant anyons serving as key physical examples. The dynamics are governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian constructed from generators of an SO(2, 1) subalgebra.
key_observables: One-point functions (e.g., expectation value of the conformal generator), state fidelity ($F$), and the trace diagnostic $T =  rac{1}{2}	ext{Tr} U(T)$.
important_parameters: Drive frequencies ($\omega_D$), modulation amplitudes ($\mu_2^0,  eta$), and the number of periods ($\ell$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of non-relativistic conformal invariance and utilizes the $	ext{SO}(2, 1)$ algebraic structure to simplify the time evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams mapping out oscillatory (elliptic) vs. exponential (hyperbolic) behavior of observables like $T$ and $\ln |F|$ as a function of drive parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the general formalism using SO(2, 1) symmetry, deriving diagnostics based on stroboscopic evolution, mapping out the three distinct dynamical phases (hyperbolic, elliptic, parabolic), and concluding with a holographic interpretation linking these phases to specific geometric structures like ergosurfaces.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful theoretical tools for analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum systems relevant to ultracold atoms. The classification of dynamical phases based on conformal symmetry is highly general and offers testable predictions for experiments involving trapped fermions near unitarity.
